newsitem.title: USA: TABLE-Arch Comms Q2 net loss widens.
newsitem.headline: TABLE-Arch Comms Q2 net loss widens.

text.p: (A) Net revenues -- service revenues plus product sales, less cost of product sales -- is the most commonly used method for reporting revenues in the paging industry.
Total revenues for the quarter were $98,729,000, up 25 percent from the year earlier level of $78,983,000.
(B) Q2 Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA), rose 30 percent. EBITDA is the standard financial performance measure for paging companies.
During the quarter Arch added 151,000 net new subscriber paging units, bringing total units in service at June 30, 1997 to 3,666,000, a 28 percent increase from units in service at June 30, 1996.

With an annualized quarterly cash flow run rate during the second quarter of $130 million, Arch lowered its debt multiple to 7.39 at June 30, 1997 from 7.49 at March 31, 1997. Leverage is defined as total debt divided by annualized current quarter EBITDA.
Net losses at Arch are largely attributable to higher levels of debt to finance growth, as well as depreciation and amortization expenses associated with network equipment, pagers and acquisitions.
